title: The speed dial: where does the lab stop moving and start fast-forwarding?
question: Watch the six panels. At which one does the box stop showing things moving and start showing jump cuts?
context_md:
The lab's speed dial is built, and this is what its six stops look like from
the player's chair. It is the last thing before the dial is called done.

**Six panels, one box.** Same bed, same seed, same warm-up, so on the first
frame they are identical. Each then runs at its own multiplier for the same
**1.2 seconds of your watching time**, drawn 20 times a second. The 1x panel
advances 1.2 seconds of world; the 256x panel advances 5 minutes of it. They
diverge because that is what the dial does, not because anything is broken --
the counts under this image show it: same box, 72 ticks run in one panel and
18,432 in another, and the plants and the colony end up in different places
because of it.

**An ant is two dark cells on dark soil and you find it by watching it move**
-- this repo has that from you, on a colony contact sheet. So a still of any one
of these panels shows you almost nothing, and the animation is the only thing
that can answer the question. If you cannot pick the ants out even in the 1x
panel, say so: that is a finding about the lab's legibility and I would rather
have it than not.

**What I already measured, so you do not have to judge it.** In this box the
only things that translate are the ants, and an ant covers **0.06 cells a
tick** -- so the obvious arithmetic (a falling grain moves a cell a tick)
overstates by about **14x**. Under 0.16% of the box changes even at 256x.

**Two defensible lines, and the panels bracket both.** An ant is 2 cells, and
"you can follow a thing while it moves less than its own width between frames"
gives either:

- the **fastest tenth** of ants crossing two cells, which is the **4x** panel
  (identical on three seeds), or
- the **typical** ant crossing two cells, which is the **16x** panel.

The game currently ships the strict one and calls 4x the last of the motion.
That is a guess about your eye, not a measurement of it, and the readout names
whichever side you put the line on -- so wherever you say it is, is where it
will say it.

items.label: The six dial stops, side by side
items.caption: top row 1x / 2x / 4x, bottom row 16x / 64x / 256x, drawn 20 times a second
